findings.summary: tryParseLink() finds the FIRST ')' after '](' to close the URL, and the FIRST ']' to close the text -- a real http(s) URL containing a literal ')' (very common: Wikipedia-style .../wiki/Foo_(bar), or any query string with an encoded-looking paren) gets its href silently truncated at that paren, with the remainder of the real URL leaking as literal trailing text; the same applies to link text containing an unescaped ']' or '('. Not exploitable for scheme bypass (verified by hand-tracing several injection attempts: the extracted url substring always starts at the literal text right after '](', so it can never be coerced into starting with 'http'/'https' unless it genuinely is one -- javascript:/data: attempts always get rejected by isSafeLinkUrl's startsWith check regardless of how the parens are arranged). This file is untouched by this diff and the bug predates it (window.prompt already fed raw text through the same insertLink/parse path), but the new dialog is the first UI surface that legitimizes users pasting real-world URLs freely, making the bug more reachable than before. Fix: Track paren/bracket depth (or require the URL segment to have no unescaped ')') in tryParseLink so a URL like https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foo_(bar) parses whole; out of scope for this ship since it is pre-existing and not in this PR's touchpoints.

validateLinkUrl() checks protocol via new URL(trimmed).protocol, which the WHATWG URL parser normalizes to lowercase -- so a user-entered 'HTTP://example.com' passes validation. But the hook (use-kudos-link-dialog.ts:134) stores and later inserts the RAW trimmed string, not the normalized parsed.href, and parse-kudo-markdown.ts's isSafeLinkUrl/isSafeHref use a case-sensitive startsWith('http://'). Net effect: an uppercase-scheme URL validates fine in the dialog but silently fails to render as a clickable link later (degrades to plain text) -- fails safe, not a security issue, just an inconsistency between the two gates. Fix: Either insert parsed.href (normalized) instead of the raw trimmed string, or make isSafeLinkUrl/isSafeHref case-insensitive to match. Low priority -- uppercase URL schemes are rare in practice.

The 'React Event Bubbling Fix' section claims both Save AND Cancel buttons call e.stopPropagation() in onClick handlers, with a code snippet showing that. The actual shipped code (kudos-compose-link-dialog.tsx) only calls stopPropagation() once, on the dialog's onCancel handler (wired to Escape / native cancel) -- the Save/Cancel BUTTON onClick handlers (onSave, onCancelClick) pass straight through with no stopPropagation wrapper. This happens to be harmless (both buttons are type="button" so they never trigger the outer <form>'s onSubmit regardless of click-bubbling, and that form's onSubmit already calls preventDefault() unconditionally), and the actual bubbling risk the note describes (React's synthetic onCancel bubbling to the outer dialog's own onCancel) IS correctly fixed at the right event -- but the evidence doc's code claim does not match the code that shipped. Fix: Correct the evidence note to describe the actual fix (stopPropagation on the nested dialog's onCancel, not on button onClick) so a future reader isn't misled about where the bubbling risk actually lived.
